target_customer: US gig workers, freelancers and small business owners who file self employed returns; later complex returns for individuals and small businesses.
problem: Freelancers miss tax write-offs and overpay; TechCrunch cited an estimated $173 per month saved on average for users.
business_model: Consumer subscription (about $14 to $16 per month) bundling write-off detection, tax filing and audit protection, with human accountants reviewing AI prep.
product_category: Consumer and small business tax filing with AI

founders.name: Paul Koullick
previous_startups: A condom donation startup built in a Harvard course (failed, per Harvard SEAS profile)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2019) names him CEO; the YC page lists David Kang as Founder/CEO, a conflict between sources.

founders.name: David Kang
prior_employers: A Chicago trading firm (quantitative modeling, per TechCrunch)
founders.background_notes: YC page: ex quantitative trader. TechCrunch says Koullick and Kang are childhood friends and former debate partners.

competitors.name: Catch
competitors.what: Another YC alum selling health insurance, retirement savings and tax withholding services to freelancers and contractors.

technical_complexity.rationale: Classifying card transactions as write-offs with ML and routing low confidence ones to human bookkeepers by text is standard applied ML plus operations; IRS e-file authorization and tax rules add hard parts later.

defensibility.rationale: Bank connections and filing history create some stickiness, but incumbents like Intuit and well funded rivals could copy write-off detection.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Keeper's own comparison pages target QuickBooks, Wave and FreshBooks, and no incumbent absorbed it; it kept growing, reporting more than 700,000 workers helped in its media kit.

market_need_then: Keeper's own materials claim about 40 million Americans overpay taxes by an average of $1,249, and TechCrunch reported 200 paying customers in March 2019 after the founders pitched rideshare drivers directly.

branding.name_origin: Keeper's 2022 rebrand post says the name reflects helping users keep more of their income, and the hope that people see the product as a keeper.
branding.domain_note: Operates on keepertax.com rather than keeper.com; acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: Rebrand introduced stars as a symbol of three values.
identity.visual_style: Blues and purples, chosen to differ from the reds and blacks of traditional tax software.
identity.voice_and_tone: Magical, approachable and honest, with upfront pricing and no ads or data selling.

branding.brand_signature: Tagline 'taxes made magical' and the star motif.

rebrands.from: Keeper 2018 era tax savings app identity
rebrands.to: Keeper identity as a full tax platform with stars, new colors and 'taxes made magical'
rebrands.why: Company says it grew from finding tax breaks into filing taxes and audit protection.

branding.community_and_virality: The company publishes customer stories and has a media kit; Trustpilot shows hundreds of reviews. No fan or meme evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear name and a considered 2022 identity, with strong customer reviews, but the generic word name is shared with other products and no independent press on the brand was found.

pivots.to: Full tax filing platform for gig, creator and freelance workers
pivots.why: The April 2021 Series A release describes building a complete tax platform; the rebrand post says it grew into a one stop tax platform.

outcome_analysis: Keeper grew from 200 paying customers in March 2019 to a reported 700,000 workers helped by its media kit, funded by a $1.65M seed from Matrix in April 2019 and a $13M Series A in April 2021. It widened from write-off detection to full filing, which raised revenue per user and defensibility. No exit or distress is reported, and the YC page today pitches AI filing for complex returns.
notes: CB Insights total of $17.66M over 6 rounds, SeedTable $14.6M and Clay $15.75M exceed the $14.65M in the two recorded rounds; a February 2020 round of $1M or $1.81M and a $150K early round appear only in aggregators and are unverified. YC lists David Kang as CEO while TechCrunch and the 2021 release name Paul Koullick CEO and founder. Keeper's comparison pages name Hurdlr, Everlance and QuickBooks but are undated marketing pages, so they are not listed as competitors at founding. Another company named Keeper rebranded to Double in October 2025 and is unrelated.
